claim: CloudTrail network activity events let VPC endpoint owners record the AWS API calls made using their VPC endpoints from a private VPC to the AWS service, for example to detect credentials from outside their organization trying to use their endpoints.
q: Which CloudTrail event type records API calls made through a VPC endpoint?
v: enable VPC endpoint owners to record AWS API calls
from a private VPC to the AWS service
ev: docs/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/logging-network-events-with-cloudtrail

CloudTrail network activity events enable VPC endpoint owners to record AWS API calls made using their VPC endpoints from a private VPC to the AWS service. Network activity events provide visibility into the resource operations performed within a VPC. For example, logging network activity events can help VPC endpoint owners detect when credentials from outside their organization attempt to access their VPC endpoints.

claim: Aggregation of data events automatically consolidates them into 5-minute summaries that show trends such as access frequency, error rates and most-used actions, so you can monitor high-volume data access without processing every individual event.
q: How can you monitor high-volume data events without handling each event?
v: access frequency, error rates, and most-used actions
ev: docs/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/aggregating-data-events

By enabling aggregation on your data events, you can efficiently monitor high-volume data access patterns without processing massive amounts of individual events. This feature automatically consolidates data events into 5-minute summaries, showing key trends like access frequency, error rates, and most-used actions.

claim: CloudTrail Insights helps identify and respond to unusual activity in API call rates and API error rates by continuously analyzing management events against a baseline of normal patterns.
q: Which CloudTrail feature detects an unusual rate of API calls or errors?
v: unusual activity associated with API call rates
normal patterns of API call volume
sc: per trail or event data store
ev: docs/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/how-cloudtrail-works

AWS CloudTrail Insights help AWS users identify and respond to unusual activity associated with API call rates and API error rates by continuously analyzing CloudTrail management events. CloudTrail Insights analyzes your normal patterns of API call volume and API error rates, also called the *baseline*, and generates Insights events when the call volume or error rates are outside normal patterns.

claim: By default, CloudTrail trails and event data stores do not log Insights events, you must configure them to log Insights events, and additional charges apply for Insights events.
q: Does a new trail log Insights events by default?
v: Additional charges apply for Insights events
sc: per trail or event data store
ev: docs/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/how-cloudtrail-works
By default, CloudTrail trails and event data stores don't log Insights events. You must configure your trail or event data store to log Insights events.
docs/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/how-cloudtrail-works
Additional charges apply for Insights events. You will be charged separately if you enable Insights for both trails and event data stores.

claim: Insights events on API call rate are generated for write management APIs, and Insights events on API error rate are generated for both read and write management APIs.
q: For which management APIs does CloudTrail Insights generate call rate and error rate events?
v: API call rate are generated for `write` management APIs
sc: per trail or event data store
ev: docs/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/how-cloudtrail-works
Insights events on API call rate are generated for `write` management APIs, and Insights events on API error rate are generated for both `read` and `write` management APIs.

claim: If Insights events are enabled on a trail and CloudTrail detects unusual activity, the Insights events are logged to a different folder or prefix in the destination S3 bucket of the trail.
q: Where are CloudTrail Insights events stored for a trail?
v: destination S3 bucket for your trail
ev: docs/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/how-cloudtrail-works
If you have Insights events enabled on a trail, and CloudTrail detects unusual activity, Insights events are logged to a different folder or prefix in the destination S3 bucket for your trail.

claim: A multi-Region trail records events in all AWS Regions that are enabled in your account and delivers the log files to an S3 bucket that you specify; a single-Region trail records events in that Region only.
q: What does a multi-Region trail record compared with a single-Region trail?
v: all AWS Regions that are enabled
records the events in that Region only
ev: docs/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/how-cloudtrail-works

When you create a multi-Region trail, CloudTrail records events in all AWS Regions that are [enabled](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/accounts/latest/reference/manage-acct-regions.html#manage-acct-regions-enable-standalone) in your AWS account and delivers the CloudTrail event log files to an S3 bucket that you specify.
docs/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/how-cloudtrail-works
When you create a single-Region trail, CloudTrail records the events in that Region only.

claim: All trails created using the CloudTrail console are multi-Region trails; you can create a single-Region trail only with the AWS CLI or the CreateTrail API operation, and that is the default when you use the CLI or API.
q: Is a trail created in the console single-Region or multi-Region?
v: All trails created using the CloudTrail console
single-Region trail using the AWS CLI
ev: docs/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-multi-region-trails

All trails created using the CloudTrail console are multi-Region trails. You can only create a single-Region trail using the AWS CLI or [`CreateTrail`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/APIReference/API_CreateTrail.html) API operation.
docs/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/how-cloudtrail-works
This is the default option when you create a trail using the AWS CLI or the CloudTrail API.

claim: As a best practice, AWS recommends creating a multi-Region trail because it captures activity in all enabled Regions; you can convert a single-Region trail to a multi-Region trail by using the AWS CLI.
q: What does AWS recommend for the Region scope of a trail?
v: we recommend creating a multi-Region trail
convert a single-Region trail to a multi-Region trail
ev: docs/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-multi-region-trails
As a best practice, we recommend creating a multi-Region trail because it captures activity in all enabled Regions.
docs/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/how-cloudtrail-works
You can convert a single-Region trail to a multi-Region trail by using the AWS CLI.

claim: With a multi-Region trail you receive CloudTrail events from all enabled Regions in a single S3 bucket and, optionally, in a CloudWatch Logs log group, and the trail settings apply consistently across all enabled Regions.
q: What are the advantages of a multi-Region trail?
v: in a single Amazon S3 bucket
apply consistently across all enabled AWS Regions
ev: docs/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-multi-region-trails
The configuration settings for the trail apply consistently across all [enabled](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/accounts/latest/reference/manage-acct-regions.html) AWS Regions.
docs/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-multi-region-trails
You receive CloudTrail events from all enabled AWS Regions in a single Amazon S3 bucket and, optionally, in a CloudWatch Logs log group.

claim: For both single-Region and multi-Region trails, you can specify an Amazon S3 bucket from any Region.
q: Must the S3 bucket of a trail be in the same Region as the trail?
v: an Amazon S3 bucket from any Region
ev: docs/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/how-cloudtrail-works
For both types of trails, you can specify an Amazon S3 bucket from any Region.

claim: Events created by Amazon CloudFront, AWS IAM and AWS STS are recorded in the US East (N. Virginia) Region, us-east-1; to keep receiving global service events outside that Region you must convert single-Region trails into multi-Region trails.
q: In which Region are IAM, STS and CloudFront events recorded, and what do single-Region trails need?
v: in the Region in which they were created
ev: docs/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-concepts
Now, events created by Amazon CloudFront, AWS Identity and Access Management, and AWS STS are recorded in the Region in which they were created, the US East (N. Virginia) Region, us-east-1.
docs/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-concepts

To continue receiving global service events outside of US East (N. Virginia), be sure to convert *single-Region trails* using global service events outside of US East (N. Virginia) into *multi-Region trails*.

claim: Organization trails must be created using the management account or a delegated administrator account, and an organization trail is automatically applied to all member accounts in the organization.
q: Which accounts can create an organization trail?
v: management account or delegated administrator account
automatically applied to all member accounts
ev: docs/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/how-cloudtrail-works

Organization trails must be created using the management account or delegated administrator account, and when specified as applying to an organization, are automatically applied to all member accounts in the organization.

claim: Member accounts can see an organization trail but cannot modify or delete it, and by default they do not have access to the trail's log files in the Amazon S3 bucket.
q: Can a member account change or delete the organization trail?
ev: docs/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/how-cloudtrail-works
Member accounts can see the organization trail, but cannot modify or delete it. By default, member accounts do not have access to the log files for an organization trail in the Amazon S3 bucket.

claim: Organization trails log events for the management account and all member accounts in the organization; the management account can assign a delegated administrator to create or manage organization trails.
q: Which accounts does an organization trail log?
v: management account and all member accounts
ev: docs/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/creating-trail-organization
Organization trails log events for the management account and all member accounts in the organization.
docs/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/creating-trail-organization
The management account for the organization can assign a delegated administrator to create new organization trails or manage existing organization trails.

claim: All organization trails created using the console are multi-Region organization trails that log events from the enabled Regions in each member account; you can create a single-Region organization trail only with the AWS CLI.
q: Is an organization trail created in the console single-Region?
v: organization trails created using the console are multi-Region
ev: docs/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/creating-trail-organization

All organization trails created using the console are multi-Region organization trails that log events from the [enabled](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/accounts/latest/reference/manage-acct-regions.html#manage-acct-regions-enable-organization) AWS Regions in each member account in the organization. To log events in all AWS partitions in your organization, create a multi-Region organization trail in each partition. You can create either a single-Region or multi-Region organization trail by using the AWS CLI.

claim: When you create an organization trail, a copy of the trail with the name that you give it is created in the member accounts of your organization.
q: What happens in member accounts when you create an organization trail?
ev: docs/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/creating-trail-organization
When you create an organization trail, a copy of the trail with the name that you give it is created in the member accounts that belongs to your organization.

claim: A CloudTrail delegated administrator is a member account that can perform the same administrative tasks in CloudTrail as the management account, with some noted exceptions, and has administrative permissions on all organization trails and event data stores.
q: What can a CloudTrail delegated administrator do?
v: a member account in an organization
ev: docs/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-delegated-administrator
A delegated administrator is a member account in an organization that can perform the same administrative tasks (except as [noted](#cloudtrail-org-tasks)) in CloudTrail as the management account.
docs/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-delegated-administrator
If you choose a delegated administrator, this member account has administrative permissions on all organization trails and event data stores in the organization.

claim: You can have CloudTrail deliver log files from multiple AWS accounts into a single Amazon S3 bucket; you update the bucket policy on the destination bucket to grant cross-account permissions to CloudTrail.
q: How do you collect CloudTrail logs from several accounts in one bucket?
v: into a single Amazon S3 bucket
ev: docs/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-receive-logs-from-multiple-accounts
You can have CloudTrail deliver log files from multiple AWS accounts into a single Amazon S3 bucket.
docs/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-receive-logs-from-multiple-accounts
Update the bucket policy on your destination bucket to grant cross-account permissions to CloudTrail.

claim: To deliver log files to an S3 bucket, CloudTrail must have the required permissions, and the bucket cannot be configured as a Requester Pays bucket.
q: Can a trail deliver logs to a Requester Pays bucket?
v: cannot be configured as a Requester Pays bucket
CloudTrail must have the required permissions
ev: docs/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/create-s3-bucket-policy-for-cloudtrail

To deliver log files to an S3 bucket, CloudTrail must have the required permissions, and it cannot be configured as a [Requester Pays](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/RequesterPaysBuckets.html) bucket.
